chapter_name: Chapter 08: Adverbs and Their Correct Positions
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn advanced placement rules for different types of adverbs, avoiding common errors like splitting infinitives or misplacing 'only' and 'enough'.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Adverbs are the spices of English grammar! But just like salt, if you put them in the wrong place, it ruins the whole dish. Change an adverb's position, and you might change the entire meaning! Let's learn the secret recipes. 🧂

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Words like 'only', 'even', and 'just' should be placed IMMEDIATELY before the word they modify. Moving them changes the meaning of the whole sentence!
examples_or_templates: ONLY she ate the pizza. (Nobody else ate it.)
She ate ONLY the pizza. (She ate nothing else, no burgers or fries.)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The word 'enough' has a very specific rule. When it modifies an adjective or an adverb, it must come AFTER it. But when it modifies a noun, it comes BEFORE it.
examples_or_templates: With Adjective: He is tall ENOUGH to ride the rollercoaster. (Not 'enough tall')
With Noun: We have ENOUGH money to buy tickets.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An infinitive is 'to + verb' (to go, to eat). In formal writing, it is usually considered poor grammar to put an adverb BETWEEN 'to' and the 'verb'. This is called a split infinitive.
examples_or_templates: Incorrect (Split): I want TO quickly FINISH my homework.
Correct: I want TO FINISH my homework quickly.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which sentence is grammatically correct regarding the use of 'enough'?
❓ Which sentence means that John did not talk to anyone else but Mary?
options: John spoke to Mary only yesterday.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the position of the adverb in this sentence: 'She is enough smart to solve the puzzle.'
subjective_practice.hint: Where does 'enough' go when modifying an adjective like 'smart'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fix the split infinitive in this sentence: 'The teacher told us to carefully read the instructions.'
subjective_practice.hint: Move the adverb so it doesn't split 'to' and 'read'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this sentence so it means that I didn't lend my bike to anyone else: 'I lent my bike to Rahul.' Use the word 'only'.
subjective_practice.hint: Place 'only' right before the person you lent it to.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🔄 The 'Only' Shifting Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write the sentence: 'I hit him in the eye yesterday.' Now insert the word 'Only' in 3 different places to create 3 completely different meanings. Explain what each new sentence means!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Place 'only' and 'even' exactly before the word they modify to avoid confusion.
⭐ 'Enough' comes AFTER an adjective/adverb (strong enough), but BEFORE a noun (enough strength).
⭐ Avoid splitting infinitives (putting an adverb between 'to' and the verb) in formal writing.
